payload.statement: RESOLVED 2026-09-04: the rejected N-0010 'Actions / ranked commercial actions' framing folds into Attention as a cross-domain surfacing and routing layer. N-0010 does not survive as its own work container. Binding terms: (1) Attention surfaces and routes; work completion happens in the owning domain, never from Overview; no approve/resolve/edit of any entity from Attention. (2) Items are DERIVED; they clear when the underlying condition clears (work done, or a justification recorded against the entity in its own domain); no dismiss and no snooze. (3) Assignment is a property of the entity, not the queue; Attention shows and filters by owner (mine / my domain / all) and does not reassign; filtering is the superuser mechanism; no separate notification system. (4) Signals group by shared entity using the existing entity graph, not inference; multiple symptoms of the same CPOR case, lineup or customer render as one situation; cross-entity clustering is future work. (5) Two signal classes: CONDITION (wrong now) and PROJECTION (will be wrong unless acted on by a computed date; value decays past that date). (6) Signal history is retained from the start; projections need learnt cycle times from our own history; items persist with lifecycle appeared/changed/resolved/expired and are not recomputed and discarded on each read. (7) The reasoning is the payload: every item shows the evidence chain, not only the conclusion. (8) Audit covers the system as well as people: record what the platform asserted, when, and from what evidence. Scope: domain modules are not redesigned; Attention composes from existing platform capability and must reuse existing projection inputs (transit history, cover, lineup planning, cycle times) rather than reimplement them; permitted domain touches are deep-link route targets with filters preserved, and a justification-recording affordance where a domain has none; a missing projection input is a separate slice — report and stop. The 2026-09-02 proposal to charter Promotions & Funding / Market & Listings / template-profile nodes as N-0010's split, and to keep ranked commercial actions as a slimmed re-chartered planned node, is not accepted. Those surfaces remain D-0008 domain architecture. No nodes chartered by this recording. Evidence: .eif/audit/NS6_D0009_20260904/OPERATOR_DECISION.md.

evidence.summary: Pre-check before password verify, constant-shape dummy PBKDF2 hash for unknown users (closes both status/body and timing enumeration channels), HMAC log keys, in-memory-only state (no cip write), bounded key count (10k) against memory exhaustion. Residual: web proxy (apps/web/src/app/api/v1/[[...path]]/route.ts) forwards client-supplied X-Forwarded-For verbatim and never sets its own, so in the documented loopback-proxy topology the per-address throttle key is attacker-controlled (spoofable/bypassable, and can be used to frame/lock out a victim IP). Implementer's own code comment already discloses this; treated as residual risk, not a criterion fail, since the per-account limit (the primary control) does not depend on address.

Threat model sound for stated scope (single-account credential stuffing). Residual risks recorded: XFF spoofing defeats per-address throttle and can DoS a shared-NAT victim address (see quality.security); single-process/in-memory counters mean a multi-worker or multi-instance deployment without a shared store would divide the effective limit by worker count (not checked against actual deployment config, out of scope for this review); counters clear on process restart; shared-IP collateral lockout is an inherent IP-throttling trade-off, not a defect.

payload.rationale: none of these are AC failures; recorded for the risk register per the brownfield/no-self-authorized-scope-expansion rule.

payload.statement: N-0074 stable address. Question: which fixed hostname should CIP live on? Options: (a) a domain Warren already owns, moved to (or added as a zone in) a free Cloudflare account, named tunnel on a subdomain such as cip.<domain>; (b) buy a new domain through Cloudflare Registrar (about USD 10 a year) and do (a); (c) keep the quick tunnel (free, no account, but the address changes on every restart and company managed Chrome blocks *.trycloudflare.com). Evidence: PILOT_TUNNEL_RUNBOOK section H (browser block), N0073_DISCOVERY.md. Assumptions: this PC stays the host for now; a cloud VM is a later, separate choice. Impact: (a)/(b) give one link users can bookmark and that company Chrome opens; optional Cloudflare Access can add an email check in front of /login at no cost for up to 50 users. Reversibility: high (delete the tunnel and DNS record). Resolving step: Warren signs in with cloudflared tunnel login on this PC; the agent never handles the Cloudflare credential. Recommendation: (a) if a domain exists, else (b).

N-0075 invite password. Question: what password does the invite email carry? Options: (a) Warren's request: a fixed password the user cannot change for now; (b) a one-time password that must be changed at first sign-in; (c) no password in the mail, a single-use set-password link that expires in 72 hours. Evidence: auth.py stores PBKDF2 hashes and has set-password; the only mailer today is the shipping digest. Impact: (a) leaves a working credential in every mailbox for as long as it exists and cannot be rotated by the user; (b) limits that to first sign-in; (c) never puts a password in mail. Reversibility: high. Recommendation: (c), else (b). Roles stay the four existing roles.

N-0078 SEO and listing quality. Question: which checks count as a listing problem? Candidate checks (Warren picks): title contains brand + model; at least N images; description present and over N words; key specs present (CPU, RAM, storage, screen); price shown and in stock; search position of our listing for named search terms on Takealot. Evidence: listing_observation keeps the raw page snapshot (spec section 8), so content checks can be re-run without re-fetching; search position needs a new fetch of the search page per term. Impact: content checks are cheap; search position adds polling load per term. Reversibility: high. Resolving step: Warren lists the checks and the search terms.

N-0079 budget ledger rules. Questions: (1) grain of a budget: per product line per quarter, per customer per quarter, or both; (2) who allocates (admin only, or planner for own lines); (3) the 50/50 policy question from the spec: is promotion support split 50/50 between ASUS and the customer by default, and does the ledger track only the ASUS half; (4) what counts as committed: case approved, or case approved and exported to the customer; (5) what counts as consumed: claim settled, or payment received. Evidence: docs/SPEC_CPOR_V1_AND_LISTING_CAPTURE_V0.md section 9.7; Budgets page shows allocation/commitment/actual not recorded; planner budget check uses the lineup-derived profit reservation. Reversibility: medium (ledger rows are history). Resolving step: Warren answers 1-5.

N-0080 profit definition. Question: which cost is the margin measured against? Options: (a) PM controlled cost (the planning cost the PM owns); (b) DAP (price to the distributor/reseller); (c) landed cost (actual cost into the country). Option (d): show all three, with one named as the headline margin. Evidence: spec section 9.3 (Warren flagged 2026-07-08); lineup and CPOR margin currently do not share one definition. Reversibility: high (a read model). Resolving step: Warren names the headline cost and whether the other two are shown.

N-0081 distributor channel and New-DAP price protection. Questions: (1) the waterfall steps for a distributor deal (rebate, disti margin, in what order and on which base); (2) how New-DAP price protection is paid: credit note per unit of distributor stock on hand at the change date, or re-invoice; (3) which stock counts: DSI stock on hand at the change date, or stock bought in the last N days. Evidence: spec section 9.1; DSI SOH has no cost column today. Reversibility: medium. Resolving step: Warren walks one real price-directive example through the steps.

payload.statement: N-0071 follow-up to D-0057 (domain rule, Warren's call; not built). Question: when an open line's strict shipped twin has shipped less than the open quantity, should totals still skip the whole open line? Evidence (cip read-only, N0071_DISCOVERY.md): 552 strict pairs; 471 open = shipped, 71 open < shipped, 10 open > shipped (904 open units). In all 552 pairs a twin has the same order_line. Options: (a) keep as built (D-0057): skip the whole open line on key match; may under-count up to 904 units still open on those 10 lines; (b) count only the open quantity above the shipped twin total (open minus shipped, floor 0); needs a per-key sum and changes every reader on the shared helper at once; (c) keep (a) and list the 10 lines to Warren for a manual check. Assumptions: the Unship sheet row is a stale snapshot of the order line, not a separate remainder line. Impact: at most 904 units across 10 lines today; zero effect on the other 542. Reversibility: high, read-side only, no fact rewrite in any option. Resolving step: Warren reviews the 10 lines against the OEM order report. Built today: (a), as accepted.

N-0071 rewrote its own predicate to an uncorrelated key lookup (0.4 s to 2.5 s). Other correlated reads over RLS tables were not surveyed; owner N-0065.

Convening: the implementation run carried backend-engineer, test-engineering-specialist and database-specialist. payload.title: Supervisor recognises a network that blocks the tunnel port and stops churning the quick tunnel
acceptance_criteria: Observed 2026-10-08: after sleep on a network that blocks outbound TCP 7844, the supervisor restarted cloudflared every 10 minutes (6 launches), changing the public link each time while no tunnel could connect

When the cloudflared log shows repeated 'dial tcp ...:7844: i/o timeout' with no registered connection, the supervisor marks the tunnel 'network blocks tunnel port (7844)' on status.json and link.html and stops restarting it; it retries with a long back-off (e.g. 30 minutes) and resumes normal checks as soon as a connection registers
No other component behaviour changes; parse check 0 errors; unit test of the detector on recorded log lines
Measured live on the blocking network: no restarts while blocked; status shows the reason

payload.stage_note: Discovery: scripts/cip-supervisor.ps1 Invoke-Tunnel restarts cloudflared when /ready has failed for 10 min (TunnelDeadMinutes). Live status 09:43: tunnel unhealthy, /ready 503, public 530, launches=7; tunnel.err.log shows only 'dial tcp 198.41.x.x:7844: i/o timeout' (ERR Unable to establish connection / Serve tunnel error pairs, cloudflared backoff up to 1m4s) and no 'Registered tunnel connection'. cloudflared writes to stderr (component Err log), Start-Component records only the Out log path.

Challenge: a restart cannot help when the network drops TCP 7844 (every new launch hits the same timeout and only changes the public link); cloudflared already retries its own connection with backoff and keeps its hostname, so holding the process is strictly better. Risk of false 'blocked': a real dead tunnel with a reachable edge does not log 7844 i/o timeouts, so the old 10-min restart still applies; a 30-min fresh attempt bounds any mis-detection. Public-check restart (publicStale) is also suppressed while blocked, since the edge is unreachable. No new process, no machine setting, no regex.

Design: Read-LogTail (last 64 KB, shared read while cloudflared writes, partial first line dropped) + Get-TunnelNetworkVerdict (plain Contains: 'Registered tunnel connection' -> connected; >= 6 lines with 'dial tcp' and '7844: i/o timeout' -> port-blocked; else unknown). Start-Component also records the Err log (ErrLog); an adopted tunnel uses the newest tunnel*.err.log. Invoke-Tunnel: /ready 200 clears blocked; otherwise port-blocked -> state 'blocked', detail 'network blocks tunnel port 7844 (outbound TCP); not restarting', no restart; after 30 min blocked (TunnelBlockedRetryMinutes) one fresh launch, then 30 min again. status.json link.blocked_reason/blocked_since/blocked_retry_at; link.html shows the reason under the link.

payload.statement: Client-IP trust for the login throttle (N-0086): the web listens on 127.0.0.1 only (supervisor-enforced), so its peers are cloudflared or local processes. The Next proxy drops every visitor-supplied client-address header (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, Forwarded, CF-Connecting-IP(v6), True-Client-IP, X-Client-IP, X-Cluster-Client-IP) and sends exactly one address upstream in X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP: CF-Connecting-IP when it is a single valid IP literal (set and overwritten by the Cloudflare edge for tunnel traffic), otherwise 127.0.0.1. The API (127.0.0.1:8001) honours X-Forwarded-For only from a loopback peer (right-most entry; uvicorn's default proxy-header trust of 127.0.0.1 gives the same answer) and keys the throttle on IPv4, IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4, other IPv6 per /64. Rejected: trusting X-Forwarded-For from the tunnel (visitor-controlled); using the TCP peer (always loopback, would make one global bucket for all tunnel users). Residual: a local process can forge CF-Connecting-IP but can already reach the API directly; all non-tunnel local traffic shares one 127.0.0.1 bucket; if the web is ever bound wider than loopback, LAN clients also share that bucket (fails closed, not open). Reversible by code revert; no data change.

Steward-write role matrix (N-0086): every write on /imports (DSI/CST/shipment pipeline steps, steward resolve/ignore/bulk/resolution-plan, batch propose/jobs), /cst-steward, /mappings, /product-master-gaps (scan, preview, apply) and /exceptions (delete, clear-all) requires steward or admin via require_roles. Job create/process/cancel/retry on /imports require admin, steward or planner at the route and then a per-template check: planners only for cpor_historical_cases and cpor_payment_evidence (create, process) plus current_lineup, unified_lineup, bulk_lineup_backfill (cancel, retry); viewers never. Reads stay sign-in only. Not changed here (deferred): customer/distributor master writes and listing-capture writes remain sign-in only. product-master-gaps /preview is read-only server-side but is gated with the write it precedes.
